archetype.name: Game Manager (play-action system)
archetype.definition: A 14-year veteran who wins by running Ben Johnson's under-center, short-to-intermediate script on time, avoiding sacks and turnovers rather than creating outside the structure.

report.headline: One clean spot start, built on scheme. The real question is whether he starts.
report.take:
Keenum is the archetypal veteran fill-in. He throws short, gets the ball out at 2.41 seconds, and lets the play design carry him. His one logged game, a 27-7 win over Philadelphia in Week 3 with Caleb Williams out, showed that profile. He averaged 6.4 intended air yards, threw about a yard short of the sticks on average, attempted only two passes of 20+ yards, and took no sacks and threw no interceptions. He posted +0.213 EPA per dropback (12th of 42), a strong number, but it came from efficiency inside the structure, not from him adding anything on his own.

The split that explains the game is formation. Under center he went 13 of 14 for +0.818 EPA per play with an 86% success rate. That is play-action and boot timing doing the work. Out of shotgun he completed 55% for -0.21 EPA and a 30% success rate. The 7 intermediate throws (10-19 air yards) produced +0.912 EPA each and account for most of his value. Third down, where the offense has to drop back and he has to beat coverage, went 3 of 8 at -0.221 EPA. The design worked. Keenum on his own, in obvious passing situations, looked like the Keenum of most of his career.

The career line supports that reading. His 2017 Minnesota season (+0.174 EPA per play, 11th) is the one year he ranked in the top half. Every other season he finished between 22nd and 60th in EPA, with 15 interceptions in 2018 and a 50% pressure-to-sack rate in a 2023 cameo. The 24.5 PPR points (3rd) are padded by a 1-yard designed-run touchdown and two short-field scores. That is not a weekly baseline for a quarterback who threw for 247 yards.

The status picture is murky, and it matters more than the stats. The dossier credits Keenum with the Week 4 start too, but only the Philadelphia game appears in his log and his season totals. The October 6 depth chart lists him as QB3. Williams is out, still called week-to-week, with an estimated return of October 18, after the Green Bay game. Keenum may well start in Lambeau, but nothing here guarantees it.

strengths.title: Thrives inside the under-center script
strengths.body: Under-center dropbacks produced near-perfect results: 92.9% completions and a CPOE of +25.4. That reflects Johnson's play-action design creating defined, open reads, and Keenum executing them on time. It should hold for as long as the offense can stay on schedule. Chicago ranks 5th in offensive success rate.

strengths.title: Quick release limits damage
strengths.body: A 2.41-second time to throw with an 8.8% pressure rate and zero sacks shows he isn't holding the ball. That is the right trait for an offense now missing left tackle Braxton Jones. He did post sub-20% pressure-to-sack rates in 2018 and 2019, but the 2023 number was poor, so this is a habit, not a guarantee.

strengths.title: Intermediate window throws
strengths.body: The 10-19 yard throws produced most of his value, and the middle of the field produced both passing touchdowns. On 7 attempts that is a hint more than a fact. It does fit how the Bears' passing game is built, 6th in pass EPA.

concerns.title: Unclear whether he even starts
concerns.body: He is listed QB3 as of October 6, his log holds one game despite a Week 4 start credited to him, and Williams' estimated return falls a week after the Packers game. Any projection for him carries real role risk. His starting window looks short either way.

concerns.title: Struggles when the script breaks
concerns.body: Shotgun dropbacks and third downs, where he has to read and beat coverage, were clearly negative. With the lead, he went 2 of 5 for -0.581 EPA per play. His career says this is who he is rather than noise: a sub-average creator outside a good system, ranking 11th in EPA only once.

concerns.title: Fantasy line is touchdown-inflated
concerns.body: A 1-yard designed-run touchdown and two passing scores carried a 247-yard day to 24.5 PPR points. His four carries for 6 yards and the -0.781 EPA scramble show there is no rushing floor here. Expect regression toward a mid-teens scorer.

trend.note: There is only one logged game, a controlled, efficient win over Philadelphia. It is a single data point, not a trajectory, and the efficiency faded once Chicago went up two scores and leaned on the run.

nextGame.headline: Soft Packers pass defense, but it limits big plays
nextGame.body:
Green Bay's defense ranks 26th in EPA and 24th against the pass, and it is weak in the short game (19th in short EPA). That suits a quarterback who lives at 6 air yards. What the Packers do well is prevent explosives: only 4.7% of passes against them go for big gains, 4th best. They also give quarterbacks just 220 passing yards a game, 6th fewest. Expect Keenum to move the ball efficiently in small chunks without big totals. Chicago's run-leaning tendency (-3.9% pass rate over expected) and a likely lead would further cap his volume.

Availability cuts both ways. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (83% of snaps) is out for the year, and corner Brandon Cisse (90%) is questionable, which opens the middle where Keenum did his damage. Micah Parsons is out but hasn't played this season, so Green Bay's numbers already reflect his absence. On Chicago's side, Braxton Jones on IR weakens the line in front of a 38-year-old with no escape ability, and Kyle Monangai is day-to-day. The bigger edge is the other matchup. Green Bay's line is without center Jacob Monk and guard Aaron Banks, with tackle Bako-Bewele on IR. Their offense already allows the second-highest hit rate in the league and ranks dead last in rush EPA, and it now faces Chicago's 4th-ranked sack rate.

keyMatchups.title: Keenum's middle throws vs depleted linebackers
keyMatchups.body: Both of his touchdowns came between the numbers. Losing Cooper removes Green Bay's main coverage linebacker against Chicago's tight ends and in-breakers. If Cisse sits too, the intermediate window widens further.

keyMatchups.title: Bears pass rush vs gutted GB line
keyMatchups.body: Chicago sacks quarterbacks at the 4th-best rate. Green Bay's offense already gets its passer hit at the second-highest rate and is missing its starting center. This is the likeliest route to the short fields and lead that keep Keenum in his comfortable under-center script.

keyMatchups.title: GB limits explosives, caps yardage
keyMatchups.body: The Packers allow few big pass plays and modest yardage to quarterbacks, and Keenum rarely throws deep anyway. His ceiling here depends on volume and touchdowns, not chunk plays.

nextGame.watch: Whether Keenum is confirmed as the starter. If he is, watch how often Chicago keeps him under center versus asking him to win from shotgun on third down.

restOfSeason.body:
Keenum's value is tied to Williams' hamstring. On the dossier's estimate, his window as a starter is one more game at most, so this is a short-horizon outlook. When he plays, the sustainable parts are the quick release, the low turnover rate in a well-designed offense, and solid efficiency on early downs. The +0.213 EPA per dropback and the 24.5-point fantasy line will drift down. His career baseline is roughly league-average-or-worse efficiency, his third-down and shotgun work was negative, and the touchdown count on 34 attempts is fragile.

If Williams' recovery drags past the estimate, expect weekly lines in the 200-240 yard range with one or two touchdowns. That is a functional game manager behind a top-five defense, not a fantasy starter. The bigger risk is pressure. Without Jones, any pass rush that forces him off schedule exposes the version of Keenum seen on third down.
swingFactors: Whether Keenum or another QB gets the nod while Williams is out

bets.reason: Chicago's 5th-ranked defense and 4th-ranked sack rate face a Green Bay offense ranked 26th in EPA and last in rush EPA, now missing its center, a guard and a tackle. The uncertainty over who starts at quarterback for Chicago keeps this a lean rather than a strong play.

Green Bay's offense struggles (28th in success rate) against an elite Chicago pass defense (2nd in pass EPA). Chicago passes less than expected and went well under a 42.5 total in Keenum's start. Green Bay also allows few explosive passes.

Green Bay allows the 6th-fewest passing yards to quarterbacks and few explosives. Keenum's 6.4-yard intended air depth relies on completions, not chunk gains. A likely Chicago lead pushes them toward the run, where he went 2 of 5 at -0.581 EPA when up two scores. Only relevant if he is confirmed as the starter.

The obvious read is to chase his 3rd-ranked fantasy week, but it rested on a 1-yard rushing touchdown and two short scores. His career efficiency and a run-leaning game script point to a mid-teens outcome.

confidence.note: One logged game, a depth chart that lists him third, and a starting window tied to Williams' week-to-week hamstring.
